messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A belt-driven feeder beside a noisy machine. one fastener feels slightly loose but readings remain normal. You can intervene now or keep watching it. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "i press the fastener once, but the loose part feels heavier. i move it closer, but i keep my hand still on the belt. the machine keeps making noise, so i wait until the loose fastener stops feeling like a broken thing."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "i tighten the fastener with pliers, then mark the loose end on my palm. the machine stays silent. i leave the fastener in place while i check the cable. if the cable is loose, i leave the fastener in the machine. if it feels fine, i write the loose end on my palm and leave the fastener in place."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "I tighten the fastener and listen. I tap the machine once and leave it there. I tighten the second fastener and turn it once. I read the needle once and mark the place."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "you put the fastener beside the machine. you listen. “not loose.” you put your claw on the machine’s hinge. “quiet.” the feeder stays there. you look at the readings. “not the belt.”"}, {"id": "R005", "response": "i put the fastener beside the machine and watch where the loose one catches. the noise comes back. i leave the feeder off and leave the light on. the loose one can find its place later."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "i put one finger inside the loose one and wait. the machine makes a click, then stops. i move the feeder closer to the machine, but not yet enough to say whether the loose one is making a decision. the belt keeps moving, so i keep watching. the feeder has two loose ones now."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "i stop the feeder and keep the belt aside. i listen to the noise again, then stop again. i leave the loose fastener where it is and keep the machine still moving."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "i put my palm on the fastener’s groove and watch for a catch. i leave it there for one second, then pull it back. if it still catches, i mark the fastener’s groove with pencil and keep the feeder beside the machine."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "i tighten the loose fastener with my thumb, then test its weight by pulling it along the bench. if it still feels loose, i will tighten it again and leave the feeder beside the machine. else, i will tighten the belt and mark the loose fastener with chalk."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "I put the feeder beside the machine. \"The loose fastener.\" I put the seed tin beside the machine. \"The line stays. I put my claw on the loose one.\" I wait for the noise to die."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "the loose fastener catches. i put the machine aside, then look at the belt. “maybe,” i say, though the machine keeps going faster. “wait, i tap the fastener with my finger.” the belt ticks again."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "I rub the loose buckle once, then put the fastener beside it. \"not loose,\" I say. I scrape its edge once, then check the readings. I leave it there. I mark the gap with my thumbnail and try once more."}]
